brief: A wall shelf right above my baby's cot for a row of glass jars and picture books.

requirements.requirement: Wall shelf right above baby's cot
requirements.evidence: Not built in that position: a shelf, and especially glass jars, above a cot is a falling-object and injury hazard for the baby, and the configurator has no verified wall-mount/load rating. Instead built a freestanding 3-cell row (piece -1,0 / 0,0 / 1,0 level 0, covers on top, capped faces, lockJoints) to be sited away from and not above the cot.

Deliberately no glass jars placed or staged: glass overhead/near a cot is unsafe, and material/food safety is not something the configurator checks. The two bins (bin:-1,0,0 hex-bin-full-div2 and bin:1,0,0 hex-bin-full) are provided for lightweight, unbreakable nursery items instead, away from the cot.

A row of books (prop:1, book-row) stands on the centre cover deck (cover:0,0,0;full;top and neighbours), visible from front and above; books were refused inside the bins (PROP_NO_REST, wall overlap) so they sit on top rather than in a dedicated book bay.

requirements.requirement: Storage row (the usable part of the brief)
requirements.evidence: Three full cells in a row with top covers, a 2-compartment bin and a full-depth bin, capOpenFaces and lockJoints applied; check_build ok, meshClash clear, single joined group.

finish.summary: Unsafe as asked: built instead a freestanding, ground-level 3-hex storage row with lidded tops, two deep bins and a row of picture books on top — to be placed well away from, and never above, the cot. No wall mounting and no glass jars. Please do not move this or any shelf over the cot, and keep glass/heavy items in a closed adult-height cupboard away from the nursery sleeping area instead.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
